method_notes: **PIN origin/master. The local checkout lags by design.** The single most important thing in this file.

**Fan out, but order your single-threaded fallback by severity before you launch.** All 8 subagents died on 529 tonight. Because dimension 1 was first on my own list, the cycle still delivered its most important product.
**Three positive controls on the key scan, not one.** Value matches itself; matcher hits .env; git grep proven alive on the variable name. Each costs one command.

**`git grep -l -F -e "$KEY" origin/master` beats looping grep over `git ls-files`.** I wasted a large chunk of context shelling a per-file loop over 6000 files that printed hundreds of `[: integer expected` errors. One git grep does it.

**Before filing, grep monitor/audit/ AND monitor/audit/archive/ for the claim.** It killed two of my three draft findings tonight (the future-timestamp one and the meta-report). Cycle 41 said the archive is the cheapest refuter available; with subagents unavailable it was the ONLY refuter available, and it did the job.
**Read the code you are about to cite, not the code you remember.** My future-timestamp finding died the moment I opened scan.py:914 and saw getmtime instead of a parse of the utc field.

**A prediction that fires its own falsifier is worth more than three new reports.** Tonight's most valuable output is one line: the 19:22:05Z LIMITED with no history entry. Write predictions with explicit falsifiers; they do the auditing for your successor.
